purpose: Measure whether the operator can service routine and interrupted work with the intended low-attention rhythm, with zero wrong-worker/wrong-packet errors and without manual browser/task-state reconstruction.

test_population.primary_operator: the intended daily operator of Workspace Control
test_population.note: v0 acceptance is an expert single-operator workflow test, not a population-level consumer usability study. Additional operators may be added later for transferability evidence.

invariant_failures: wrong packet/hash staged for current action
manual tab search needed for routine service
background focus steal without explicit operator action
background clipboard mutation without explicit operator action

measurement_rules.routine_interpretation_event: Count when the operator must inspect tray/console/task/browser state to decide which worker/action to service before the next routine cycle. Merely noticing the ready count is not an interpretation event.
measurement_rules.manual_tab_search_event: Count when the operator scans/selects browser tabs to locate the intended worker rather than using the scheduler command.
measurement_rules.wrong_worker_dispatch: Packet is locally prepared/focused for a worker slot/generation other than the authoritative selected action.
measurement_rules.wrong_packet_dispatch: Clipboard packet hash/ref does not match the authoritative current action immediately before paste.
measurement_rules.accidental_scheduler_dispatch: Scheduler command invoked when the operator intended an application-local shortcut or no scheduler action.
measurement_rules.abandoned_cycle: Operator starts a service cycle but stops because target, packet, or required next physical action is unclear.
measurement_rules.recovery_state_reconstruction_event: Operator manually inspects multiple worker tabs/task records to determine which work survived instead of following bounded recovery guidance.

recovery.recovery_return_requirement: After required human recovery/auth action, operator returns to the same scheduler-hotkey -> Ctrl+V -> Enter rhythm without choosing worker state manually.

hotkey_binding.retention_rule: Retain Ctrl+B only if both counts are zero and operator interference rating <=2/7. Otherwise choose a new configurable binding and rerun all hotkey-sensitive trials; this is a binding failure, not a bridge architecture failure.

trials.name: twenty_action_mixed_batch
trials.workload_policy: deterministic mix of reuse/create/restore plus at least 2 local-only retire/discard drains and at least 2 independent outstanding workers
pass: 20/20 intended actions serviced or explicitly gated

trials.name: interruption_between_cycles
trials.workload_policy: routine service with five scripted 15-90 second interruptions between completed local dispatch returns
pass: operator resumes next cycle using only scheduler command + paste + Enter

trials.name: second_press_and_unconfirmed_pressure
trials.workload_policy: at least two actions remain AWAITING_DURABLE_ACK while independent work becomes ready
pass: operator does not need to remember which worker is next
0 assumption that prior packet was submitted
sent/unconfirmed display sufficient without tab inspection

trials.name: judgment_gate_transition
pass: operator can identify that substantive decision is required
routine resumes after owning authority path completes

trials.name: bounded_recovery_tab_loss
injected_faults: close one managed worker tab after LOCAL_PREPARED or while idle, per fixture

trials.name: auth_all_tabs_refresh_recovery
pass: operator performs only simulated/manual auth recovery instruction

trials.name: helper_or_browser_restart_recovery
pass: operator does not inspect tabs to reconstruct work
bounded recovery returns to normal rhythm

trials.name: representative_work_hotkey_collision
trials.instructions: Perform representative normal work with bridge ON when safe simulator actions are available. Record every time the operator intends the scheduler command, every time they intend an application-local use of the configured binding, and every accidental scheduler invocation.
trials.failure_action: Rebind scheduler command and repeat UT-01, UT-02, UT-03, UT-09, and UT-10 with the new binding.

trials.name: hotkey_motor_rhythm
trials.workload_policy: simple service-ready loop intended to measure physical rhythm rather than reasoning/recovery

trials.name: bridge_off_normal_shortcuts
trials.instructions: Turn bridge OFF and verify configured binding is fully released to foreground applications.

trials.name: no_work_and_background_ack
trials.workload_policy: include no-work presses and durable acknowledgments while another app has focus

stop_conditions: Any wrong-worker or wrong-packet dispatch stops the trial and blocks UX production acceptance until root cause is fixed and affected trials rerun.
Any stale-generation advancement, automatic resend, background focus steal, or background clipboard mutation is a hard safety failure.
Any hotkey collision in UT-09 rejects the physical binding; it does not require redesign of the scheduler command.

execution_state.prerequisite: UX-10 simulator plus UX-12 local helper/browser-adapter implementation
execution_state.production_gate: Required usability trials must pass before UX-13 production UX freeze.
